scenes.headline: Cloud SDK with boto3 (S3)
scenes.subtitle: Programmatic access to AWS storage
scenes.narration: boto3 is the official AWS SDK for Python, and it is the tool data engineers reach for to read, write, and manage the objects in S3 that form the backbone of most cloud data lakes.

scenes.headline: client vs resource
items: client gives low-level, one-to-one mappings to AWS API calls
resource offers a higher-level, object-oriented abstraction
Most modern code and all newer services favor the client
scenes.narration: boto3 exposes two interfaces, and knowing the difference saves confusion. The client is a thin, low-level wrapper that maps directly onto AWS API operations and returns raw dictionaries. The resource layer wraps those calls in convenient Python objects like Bucket and Object. In practice most current code uses the client, since it covers every service and newer features often land there first.

scenes.headline: Uploading and downloading objects
scenes.code:
import boto3

s3 = boto3.client("s3")

s3.upload_file("local.parquet", "my-bucket", "data/2024/local.parquet")

s3.download_file("my-bucket", "data/2024/local.parquet", "copy.parquet")

obj = s3.get_object(Bucket="my-bucket", Key="data/2024/local.parquet")
body = obj["Body"].read()
scenes.narration: After creating a client, upload_file and download_file handle the common case of moving whole files, transparently managing multipart transfers for large objects. When you want the bytes in memory instead of on disk, get_object returns a streaming body you read directly. Notice that the key includes a path-like prefix, which is how S3 mimics folders even though it is really a flat key-value store.

scenes.headline: Paginating large listings
scenes.narration: S3 returns at most a thousand keys per list request, so naively calling list_objects on a large prefix silently misses data. The paginator solves this cleanly by handling the continuation tokens for you and yielding one page at a time. Iterating over the Contents of each page lets you walk millions of objects without ever holding the full listing in memory.

scenes.headline: Credentials & configuration
items: Never hardcode keys; use IAM roles or environment variables
boto3 resolves credentials through a standard provider chain
Configure region and retries via config or the AWS config file
scenes.narration: Hardcoding access keys is the cardinal sin of cloud engineering, so lean on IAM roles when running in AWS and environment variables or profiles elsewhere. boto3 automatically searches a well-defined credential provider chain, checking environment, shared files, and instance metadata in order. Region and retry behavior are best set once in configuration rather than scattered through your code.

scenes.text: Use the client, paginate every listing, and let IAM manage credentials — never hardcode secrets.
scenes.narration: Default to the low-level client, always paginate when listing objects at scale, and delegate authentication to IAM roles and the provider chain. Those three habits keep boto3 code both correct and secure.
